learning: If the oval finish rate rises above 0.45 and s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m, turn authority is still the lever and the next step is a small kp trim. If max_error stays at about 0.063 m with no completion gain, the limit is base_speed (controller side), so I will lower or raise it next rather than change geometry. If steering_oscillation rises well above 0.43 on the s-bend, kd is the next lever.
notes: Builder's wheel_track 0.09 m package. kp is scaled down by about 1.11x (3.6 to 3.3) to hold the effective yaw gain steady after the track narrows. kd 0.6 and ki 0.2 are kept from iteration 2, and base_speed 1.4 is held so the race isolates turn authority.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the best result so far (321). Its gain came from the oval, where finish rate rose from 0.05 to 0.45. Iteration 1 showed that widening the sensor row cut line loss (s-bend 1.1 to 0.2) but still ended every run off track, so sensing is not the binding limit. Max_error sits at about 0.06 to 0.063 m in every trial of every design, which points to turn response. The Builder's geometry narrows wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.09 m with mass 0.6 kg, the five-sensor row at ±0.04 m, and the body unchanged. Turn rate is (v_R - v_L)/wheel_track, so for the same PWM difference the yaw rate rises by about 0.10/0.09 = 1.11x. To keep the effective steering gain at the level that produced iteration 2, I scale kp down by the same factor: 3.6/1.11 ≈ 3.3. I keep ki at 0.2 and kd at 0.6 (the iteration 2 damping, which kept steering_oscillation at 0.27 on the oval and 0.43 on the s-bend). base_speed stays at 1.4 and line_loss stays 'last_direction', so this race isolates the geometry change. Expected result (a prediction, not a measurement): higher yaw response, more s-bend completions and max_error below 0.06 m. The main risk is steering_oscillation rising on the s-bend, which the kd of 0.6 should limit.
